summary.text: A natal female identifying as male was diagnosed with POTS in November 2014 at age 16 years after a 1 year history of dizziness and headaches, with subsequent fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, insomnia, early satiety, numbness, joint pain, palpitations, tachycardia and other symptoms. Findings included venous pooling and joint hypermobility, with hypermobile Ehlers–Danlos syndrome in his history and a heart rate rise from 95 to 135 beats per minute on 10-min stand.

He was treated with cyproheptadine, fludrocortisone and pregabalin for his three worst symptoms; the headaches resolved, but dizziness persisted despite fludrocortisone, midodrine and desmopressin, and pain did not respond to pregabalin or duloxetine.

He was seen in the Gender and Sexuality Clinic 1.5 years after his POTS diagnosis, was diagnosed with gender dysphoria, and started testosterone therapy. Subsequent testosterone levels were in the low-normal physiological male range.

In November 2018, 4 years after the POTS diagnosis and 2 years after testosterone was started, he had no complaints of headaches or dizziness and was off all blood pressure supportive therapies. His blood pressure was elevated at 140/80 mmHg and was treated with metoprolol, and he continued to have pain attributed to joint hypermobility associated with Ehlers–Danlos syndrome.

summary.text: A natal female identifying as male was diagnosed with POTS in March 2017 at age 17 years after a 5 year history of dizziness with onset after menarche, followed by blurry vision, syncope, fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, insomnia, headache, gastrointestinal symptoms, palpitations, tachycardia and other symptoms. Venous pooling and joint hypermobility were noted, with resting blood pressure 116/65 mmHg and a heart rate rise from 70 to 105 on 10 min stand.

He was treated with cyproheptadine, fludrocortisone and pyridostigmine for his three worst symptoms and referred for physical therapy. Headaches and early satiety improved and he started routine exercise, but dizziness remained uncontrolled despite fludrocortisone and desmopressin, and a higher pyridostigmine dose for persistent constipation caused muscle twitching, so the dose was reduced.

He was seen in the Gender and Sexuality Clinic in February 2019, 2 years after POTS diagnosis, was diagnosed with gender dysphoria and started testosterone therapy. In March 2019, resting blood pressure was 117/72 on low dose midodrine with a heart rate increase from 72 to 102 beats per minute on 10 min stand, and he continued cyproheptadine, pyridostigmine and salt capsules.

summary.text: A natal female identifying as male was diagnosed with POTS in July 2015 at age 16 years, with a 10 year history of migraine and subsequent dizziness, blurred vision, fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, insomnia, palpitations, tachycardia and other symptoms. Resting blood pressure was 104/72 with a persistent heart rate increase of 70–140 beats per minute on 10 min stand, and venous pooling was noted; the rest of the examination showed no abnormalities.

He was started on desmopressin for dizziness, lansoprazole for symptoms of gastroesophageal reflux and methylphenidate for fatigue, and began exercising regularly. Persistent dizziness required increased desmopressin and added midodrine, symptoms improved with regular exercise, and stimulant therapy was discontinued in 2016. A concussion in February 2017 worsened dizziness and fatigue and limited exercise.

In May 2017 he was seen in the Gender and Sexuality Clinic, was diagnosed with gender dysphoria and started testosterone therapy. Dizziness, insomnia, fatigue, headache and cognitive dysfunction all significantly improved by report, and symptoms returned when there were gaps in testosterone therapy. Testosterone levels were in the normal physiological male range.

In March 2019, resting blood pressure was 122/68 on midodrine and desmopressin. He was exercising regularly with only rare dizziness and no complaints of palpitations, dyspnea, chest pain or syncope, and the plan going forward included discontinuing desmopressin.
